understanding.what_is_being_built: An authority-grade, very large (≈3,400 pages) information site at whatisayurveda.com, whose information architecture and content priorities are to be driven by a rigorous SEO/AEO demand model across Ayurveda entities (herbs, formulations, concepts, treatments, classical texts, conditions, etc.).
understanding.why: To choose what to build first, how deep to go, and how to structure clusters so the site captures real search demand and intent in key markets (US and India) and supports best-in-class AEO answers. This demand layer is the foundation for the content roadmap and IA.
understanding.intended_structure: Entity-clustered taxonomy (as shown in the artifact: herbs, formulations, concepts, treatments, texts, conditions), with each entity and its intents/questions fueling topic hubs and pages. The pipeline expects entity ontology → seed list → multi-locale demand pull → plausibility checks → intent/difficulty/opportunity scoring → IA and content outlines.
understanding.decision_tree: Per the artifact’s own supersession note, the correct process is: build an explicit entity ontology; use real single-term canonical seeds and synonyms; pull demand for multiple locales/languages (including Hindi/Devanagari/Hinglish for India); run automated plausibility validation; ground with external sources (Perplexity, SERP checks); add intent/difficulty/opportunity scoring before any content decisions. The detailed MASTER_PIPELINE.md is referenced but not provided here.

recommendations: Freeze any IA/content work dependent on this file. Nothing proceeds until a re-run passes all gates.

Run Step 3 correctly per MASTER_PIPELINE: (1) Build an explicit Ayurveda entity ontology (herbs, formulations, therapies, body concepts, classical texts, conditions), with canonical names, synonyms/transliterations (e.g., amla/amalaki, guduchi/giloy, shallaki/boswellia), and schema.org alignments where applicable.
Generate single-term seed lists from the ontology; forbid concatenated dual-name seeds. Deduplicate by canonical entity; preserve synonym mappings for later matching.
Multi-market, multi-language pulls: US-en; India: en + hi (Devanagari) + common Hinglish variants. Consider additional Indian languages only if in scope; document choices.

Implement automated plausibility validation: flag zeros for high-profile entities; detect unlikely market skews; cap outliers; run trend sanity checks; require human spot-check on the top 200 terms across two independent sources (GKP + Ahrefs/Semrush). Commit the validation report.

Add AEO/intent research: extract PAA/Related/‘People also search’ and YouTube/Reddit Qs per entity; map intents (definitional, benefits, dosage, side effects, interactions, preparation, comparisons, contraindications).
Add difficulty/opportunity scoring: capture KD/competition strength, SERP feature mix, DR of ranking pages, and topical gap vs named competitors. Produce a composite priority score per entity/intent.

Compile the competitor set empirically from SERPs across representative queries (e.g., ashwagandha, panchakarma, chyawanprash, ‘what is ayurveda’). Log who ranks, content models, and SERP features. Commit this to docs/whatisayurveda-research/competitors.md.

Publish proof-of-work: commit raw DataForSEO JSON (with timestamps and query params), script outputs (including scripts/audit-gpt.mjs results), and the plausibility-validation logs to the repo. No self-reported success.

Acceptance criteria before greenlighting IA/content: ≥1,000 canonical entities/intents covered; Hindi/Hinglish incorporated for India; 0 inexplicable zeros on top-200; ≤2% duplicate synonyms unresolved; ≥95% of top-200 spot-checked across two sources; priority scoring present; competitor/intent layers documented.
Only after the above passes, produce the 3,400-page IA and content outline packs per cluster, with AEO questions and compliance notes (YMYL flags requiring clinical review where applicable).
